value.body: A CNC programmer creates the programs that run computer-controlled lathes and machining centres, turning engineering drawings into finished parts. Machine shops, auto-component makers, tool rooms and aerospace and die-mould suppliers hire for this work. A typical day involves reading drawings, preparing programs in CAM software, setting up tools and proving out first parts with operators.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech/B.E. (Production or Mechanical) or a diploma

items.label: Common tools
items.value: CAM software, G-code, CNC lathes and machining centres

items.label: Auto-component industry turnover
items.note: Whole industry; one of the main users of CNC machining

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often start as trainee programmers or setters in machine shops and tool rooms, learning on real machines. Hands-on CAM and CNC training from a tool room or training centre is commonly valued.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: senior programmer, process engineer, tool-room or production in-charge.
Hands-on shop-floor work, often in shifts.
Skills carry across auto, aerospace and die-mould work.
